problems.problem: Over-drainage in upright posture — P_venous drops when patient stands, increasing dP, causing excessive CSF drainage and intracranial hypotension
Under-drainage during venous congestion — P_venous rises during Valsalva, sleep apnea, or venous sinus stenosis, reducing dP and causing inadequate drainage
Fixed threshold doesn't adapt to patient physiology — ICP 'normal' varies by patient, age, disease state; a fixed threshold over/under-drains for many patients
Nocturnal ICP variation — ICP rises during REM sleep; passive valve may under-drain at night, leading to morning headaches and progressive ventriculomegaly
Acute decompensation detection — sudden ICP rise (hemorrhage, obstruction) requires immediate drainage increase; passive valve responds too slowly
